benefits: Solves the whole triangle — area, all three angles, perimeter and type — from just three sides.
Validates the triangle inequality and explains clearly when sides cannot form a triangle.
Classifies the triangle by sides and by angles automatically.
Also gives the circumradius and inradius, useful for geometry problems.
Everything is computed locally in your browser.

faqs.a: Three lengths form a triangle only if the sum of any two is greater than the third: a + b > c, a + c > b, b + c > a. If any check fails — for example sides 1, 2, 10 — no triangle exists.
faqs.q: How do I know if three sides make a valid triangle?

faqs.a: Use Heron's formula: with semiperimeter s = (a+b+c)/2, area = √(s(s−a)(s−b)(s−c)). It works for any triangle when you know all three sides.
faqs.q: How is the area calculated from three sides?

faqs.a: The law of cosines: for the angle opposite side a, cos(A) = (b² + c² − a²) / (2bc), then A = arccos of that value. Repeat for each angle.
The circumradius R = abc / (4 × area) is the radius of the circle passing through all three vertices. The inradius r = area / s is the radius of the circle touching all three sides from inside.
faqs.q: What are the circumradius and inradius?

faqs.a: By sides: equilateral (all equal), isosceles (two equal), scalene (none equal). By angles: right (one 90°), obtuse (one > 90°), acute (all < 90°). A triangle gets one label from each group.
faqs.q: What do the triangle classifications mean?

triangle-calculator.formula:
Semiperimeter: s = (a + b + c) / 2
Heron's formula: Area = √(s(s − a)(s − b)(s − c))

Law of cosines (angle A opposite side a):
cos(A) = (b² + c² − a²) / (2bc)

Circumradius: R = abc / (4 × Area)
Inradius:     r = Area / s

Valid only if: a + b > c, a + c > b, b + c > a
howTo: Enter the three side lengths a, b and c.
The tool checks the triangle inequality automatically.
Read the area, perimeter and all three angles in the results.
Check how the triangle is classified — by sides and by angles.
Use the circumradius and inradius for circle-related geometry.
keyFacts: Any triangle is fully determined by its three side lengths (SSS congruence).
The three interior angles always add up to exactly 180°.
Heron's formula finds the area from sides alone — no height needed.
The longest side is always opposite the largest angle.
The 3-4-5 triangle is the most famous: a right triangle with area 6.

limitations: Only solves triangles from three sides (SSS) — not from angles or mixed inputs.
Side-equality checks use a small tolerance; near-degenerate inputs may classify unexpectedly.
Degenerate “flat” triangles (a + b = c) are rejected as invalid.
Angles are in degrees; radian output is not provided.
